architecture.runtime_volume: The existing solver-conforming Single Layer Water core now resolves a Futaleufu-only V3 material instance from the cooked-field identity when an older runnable map does not serialize the new override. Newly regenerated maps persist the same material and texture references.
architecture.runtime_detail: A project-owned flow normal replaces the inherited South Fork normal on the optical core and thin Default Lit detail surface. A project-owned foam-lace mask breaks up the rapid-foam mesh only after multiplication by solver-owned aeration and wet geometry.
architecture.capture_water: Future filtered generation creates a translucent Default Lit capture ribbon with physical IOR 1.333 and CPU-authored depth, bank-feather, and solver-aeration vertex opacity. The retained runnable map package and its historical fixed captures remain byte-identical to the baseline to avoid absorbing unrelated in-progress terrain generation.
architecture.authority_boundary: Both image-generated textures are visual-only. Solver fields, wet/dry ownership, river coordinates, live mesh topology, collision, buoyancy, bathymetry, raft forces, feature forcing, and rapid detection remain unchanged.

visual_comparison.method: Direct sRGB metrics over rows 260 through 719 of the identical 1280x720 breaking_water_side camera. Highlight fractions use normalized luminance thresholds 0.90 and 0.95.
visual_comparison.verdict: Retain as a bounded river-local optical improvement: V3 reduces the broad chalk-white response, increases cold-water color separation, and replaces the repeated foam breakup with sparser irregular lace. The sun reflection and large smooth right-hand face remain overexposed and sheet-like, so this is not photoreal acceptance.

The large right-hand standing-wave face remains too smooth and sheet-like; it lacks entrained-air depth, crest breakup, and small-scale spray.
The foam lace is visually improved but remains a generated breakup mask rather than rapid-specific observed foam calibration.
Bank geometry, ground material, vegetation silhouettes, rocks, atmosphere, and distance detail remain visibly procedural and blockout-quality.
No raft or passengers are framed in this water-only comparison, so visual raft/person occlusion still requires a dedicated production-art review even though the native render guard passes.
Named Terminator holes, rollers, rock-contact plumes, mist, recovery features, and complete-run water continuity remain incomplete or externally unaccepted.
